tasks.name: Implement GraphQL queries and HTTP communication in JobberClient
tasks.description: Implement the core GraphQL query execution logic in JobberClient using requests library. This includes constructing proper GraphQL queries for clients and invoices with cursor-based pagination, making HTTP POST requests to Jobber API, and handling HTTP response processing.
tasks.notes: Focus on HTTP communication mechanics and GraphQL query structure. Error handling will be enhanced in next task. Use exact field names from Jobber API documentation.

relatedFiles.description: Add GraphQL queries and HTTP request implementation

tasks.implementationGuide:
1. Import requests library
2. Define API_URL constant: https://api.getjobber.com/api/graphql
3. Implement GraphQL query strings for clients and invoices with cursor pagination
   - clients query: id, firstName, lastName, emails, phones, createdAt
   - invoices query: id, client{id}, invoiceNumber, amounts{total}, invoiceStatus, issuedDate
4. Implement HTTP request logic:
   - Use requests.post(API_URL, headers=auth_provider.get_headers(), json=payload)
   - payload format: {"query": query_string, "variables": {"cursor": cursor}}
5. Handle response processing:
   - Check response.status_code
   - Parse response.json()
   - Return raw dict response for EntityMapper processing
6. Basic error handling for HTTP failures
tasks.verificationCriteria: JobberClient can execute GraphQL queries to Jobber API, handles cursor-based pagination variables, returns raw dict responses, uses AuthProvider headers for authentication, and successfully communicates with https://api.getjobber.com/api/graphql endpoint.

tasks.summary: Successfully implemented GraphQL queries and HTTP communication in JobberClient with complete cursor-based pagination, proper field mapping, authentication integration, and HTTP error handling. Implementation includes API endpoint constant, structured GraphQL queries for clients and invoices, and robust HTTP request logic using requests library.

tasks.name: Add comprehensive error handling to JobberClient
tasks.description: Implement robust error handling in JobberClient for HTTP failures, authentication errors, network issues, and GraphQL errors. Map all failure scenarios to appropriate domain exceptions (JobberApiError, ConfigurationError) following established error handling patterns from Phase 1.
tasks.notes: Critical for production robustness. Follow AuthProvider error handling patterns. Provide actionable error messages for troubleshooting.

relatedFiles.description: Add comprehensive error handling throughout HTTP request methods
Domain exception classes for error mapping
Reference for error handling patterns and ConfigurationError usage

tasks.implementationGuide:
1. Import JobberApiError and ConfigurationError from ..exceptions
2. Add HTTP status code error handling:
   - 401/403 -> ConfigurationError ("Invalid or expired JOBBER_TOKEN")
   - 4xx/5xx -> JobberApiError with descriptive messages
   - Network errors (requests.RequestException) -> JobberApiError
3. Add GraphQL error handling:
   - Check response["errors"] field
   - Map GraphQL errors to JobberApiError with error details
4. Add timeout handling:
   - Set reasonable timeout values (connect=10, read=30)
   - Handle timeout exceptions -> JobberApiError
5. Add response validation:
   - Validate JSON structure
   - Check for required fields (data, clients/invoices)
   - Handle malformed responses -> JobberApiError
6. Comprehensive error messages with context
tasks.verificationCriteria: JobberClient properly handles all error scenarios with appropriate domain exceptions, provides descriptive error messages, handles network failures gracefully, maps HTTP status codes correctly, and validates GraphQL responses robustly.
